text: A hidden wire beneath her winter coat. A deadly dinner with her best friend.
Their investigation led them directly to Amy Loughren—a skilled intensive care nurse and Charles Cullen's closest confidante.
When we secretly met Amy Loughren outside the facility and laid Cullen's printed Pyxis access logs before her, she was utterly stunned.
What made her position perilous was her personal vulnerability: a single mother battling severe cardiomyopathy that endangered her own life.
Terrified as I was for my own survival and my children's future, I knew staying silent would make me complicit in his murders.
Amy Loughren entered the restaurant wearing a covert transmitter carefully concealed beneath her winter sweater by state detectives.
With immense psychological dexterity, Amy gently broached the hospital anomalies and offered to help him find a way out.
He slumped forward over the table, whispering words captured clearly on tape: “I want to stop, I want it all to be over.”
He confessed to administering lethal doses of Digoxin and Insulin to Father Florian Gall, Michael Strenko, and dozens of others over the years.
